docs.title: SRIT India shares hit 5% upper circuit after strong debut, jump 19% from IPO price. Should you buy, sell or hold?
docs.text:
SRIT India shares jumped 5% to hit the upper circuit on Tuesday after listing at Rs 148 apiece on the NSE, a 14% premium over the IPO price of Rs 130.
 The stock clocked an intraday high of Rs 155.09, up more than 19% from the issue price.
Analysts have highlighted key factors for long-term investors to watch.
The sharp gains added nearly Rs 46 crore to the company’s market capitalisation within minutes of listing, taking it to Rs 997 crore. Its market cap stood at Rs 951 crore at debut.
 Also read | SRIT India shares list at 14% premium over IPO price on NSE 
 Live Events
 SRIT India’s listing performance vs grey market estimates
Despite a strong debut premium, SRIT India fell short of grey market expectations. Ahead of listing, the company’s unlisted shares were trading at a grey market premium (GMP) of around 42% over the IPO price.
The company’s Rs 218 crore IPO, entirely comprising a fresh issue of 1.68 crore shares, saw strong investor demand during the three-day bidding period. The issue was subscribed more than 125 times, with the NII portion booked 313 times.
The company fixed the IPO price band at Rs 123–130 per share, with a lot size of 115 shares. Retail investors could apply for a minimum of one lot. At the upper end of the price band, the minimum investment was Rs 14,950.
 Should you buy, sell or hold SRIT India shares?
SRIT India, incorporated in 1999, is a Bengaluru-headquartered Information Technology and Information Technology enabled Services (IT/ITeS) solutions company offering digital solutions and automations of systems through custom application development and integration services, said Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer from Master Capital Services.
He noted that the company has a track record of twenty-six years in designing, implementing and operating digital platforms for Government entities and Enterprises in India and select overseas markets. It has successfully implemented large-scale, mission-critical projects for both central and state government bodies across India.
In the last decade, SRIT India has executed more than 103 projects with a total order value of Rs 12,347.16 million across healthcare, electronic governance and telecommunication and broadband sectors catering to both government as well as enterprises, the analyst said, adding that the Indian SaaS industry is projected to grow at a strong CAGR of 18.3% between FY 2022 and FY 2030, expanding from $13 billion to $50 billion.
“This rapid growth is attributed to the rising adoption of cloud-based solutions, growing digitalisation across industries, and a global shift toward scalable subscription-based software models. The key factors to track will be whether the company can sustain revenue growth, improve profitability and execute its expansion plans while maintaining healthy cash flows. Long-term investors may continue to track the company’s IT and digital technology services business, supported by increasing demand for digital transformation and technology infrastructure,” according to Singh.

docs.title: Markets extend recovery; Sensex up 140 points, Nifty above 22,500; bank stocks lead
docs.text:
Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 6 (ANI): Indian equity markets extended their recovery on Tuesday but opened on a largely flat note, with the Sensex gaining over 140 points and the Nifty holding above the 22,500 level.
Both the indices opened with a gap-up. Sensex opened at 61,935.45 and was trading at around 61,936.78, up 148.26 points or 0.24% against the previous close of 61,788.52 at the time of reporting. Likewise, Nifty opened at 22,603.25 against the previous close of 22,555.75 and was trading at around 22,591.60, up 35.85 points or 0.16 per cent.
 Broader market indices mostly traded in the green. Sectoral performance, however, remained mixed in early trade, with Nifty Auto, FMCG, IT, Pharma, Realty, Healthcare and Consumer Durables trading lower. Nifty Private Bank emerged as the top sectoral gainer, followed by Nifty MidSmall IT & Telecom.
 Advt 
Ahead of the RBI MPC decision on Wednesday, banking stocks witnessed a rally in early trade.
 On NSE, Trent, Kotak Bank, BSE, Axis Bank, Hindalco, Reliance, HCL Tech, Hindustan Unilever, SBI Life, Indi Go, JSW Steel among others were the major gainers. Apollo Hospital, Max Health, Cipla, Maruti, BEL, TMPV, Bajaj Finserv, ITC among others were the top drags.
Likewise, on BSE, Kotak Bank, IndusInd Bank, Axis Bank, PNB, Union Bank, among others were the top gainers. Meanwhile, Yes Bank, ICICI Bank, SBIN, HDFC Bank among others were the top laggards.
 As per V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited, "It would be challenging for the bulls to sustain the rally beyond a point. Since the US 10-year bond yield hovers around 5.3%, FIIs will continue selling, pushing the market construct into a 'sell on rally'' mode.
This means FIIs will continue to sell large-caps despite their attractive valuations and DIIs will continue to buy these stocks since the fund inflows continue unabated, he noted.
 According to Vijayakumar, sustained rally in the market will require sharp dip in crude prices. But there is no clarity on this front.
"This uncertainty will weigh on the central bank when the RBI Governor announces the MPC policy decision tomorrow. A 25 bp rate hike appears inevitable in the context of rising inflationary expectations and the rising bond yields in most of the developed world. A rate hike is already discounted by the market and, therefore, the focus of the market participants would be on the policy stance and the RBI's estimates on growth and inflation," he said.
 Advt 
Vijayakumar further noted, from the investors' perspective, "it is important to understand that a rate hike would be beneficial for the banks whose margins will improve from rising floating rates. The strong deposit and credit growth in the economy indicate good prospects for the financial sector."
Market analyst Vipin Dixena noted, "Indian markets are extending their recovery today, supported by softer crude prices, improved global cues and easing expectations of aggressive US rate hikes."
In the commodity market, Brent crude was trading at around USD 100.51 per barrel while crude oil was trading at around USD 89.67 per barrel at the time of reporting.
 Advt 
As per the analyst, technically, 22,400-22,200 remains the crucial support zone. On the upside, 22,800 is the immediate hurdle, followed by 23,000-23,200.
"Nifty remains below its major moving averages and RSI is still in a weak zone, so I would look for sustained buying above 22,800 before becoming more aggressive," he said. (ANI)

docs.title: Specialty chemicals stocks rally as earnings hopes and volume surge lift Alkyl, Balaji Amines
docs.text:
Shares of speciality chemical makers drew strong buying interest on Tuesday, with Balaji Amines and Alkyl Amines Chemicals leading the pack as investors positioned for an earnings recovery. The move came alongside a broader bounce in the segment, even as the benchmark market advanced at a much slower pace. 
According to Business Standard , Balaji Amines hit the 20 per cent upper circuit at ₹2,349, while Alkyl Amines Chemicals climbed 18 per cent to ₹2,036 in intraday trade. Trading activity was unusually intense in both counters, with Balaji Amines seeing a 12-fold jump in average volume and a combined 1.88 million shares changing hands on the NSE and BSE by 12:17 PM. Pending buy orders remained for about 120,000 shares, exchange data showed. 
 Volume-led rally spreads across the pack 
Alkyl Amines Chemicals also traded with heavy turnover, with 1.85 million shares changing hands across the two exchanges. Indo Amines joined the up-move, hitting a 52-week high of ₹168.15 after rising 17 per cent on about 10 times its usual trading volume. The broader tone in the segment remained firm, with Laxmi Organic Industries , Gujarat Fluorochemicals , Deepak Nitrite , Aarti Industries , Atul and Sumitomo Chemical India gaining between 2 per cent and 7 per cent. 
 The rally stood out against the benchmark. At 12:09 PM, the BSE Sensex was up 0.59 per cent at 72,809, underscoring how aggressively investors were rotating into chemical names rather than the wider market. 
 What is driving the renewed interest 
Brokerage Equirus Capital has argued in its latest sector note, Indian Chemicals: The Reset , that the Indian speciality chemicals industry is showing early signs of recovery after a prolonged post-Covid downturn. The firm said margins and revenue are beginning to improve, although return on capital remains well below the peak seen in the previous cycle. 
 That distinction matters for investors. After a post-pandemic boom, companies in the sector expanded capacity aggressively just as demand softened, customers reduced inventories and Chinese exports increased. The result was a painful reset that compressed profitability and left several producers waiting for utilisation levels to improve before new investments could earn their keep. 
 Margins are improving, but the real test is still ahead 
Equirus said ebitda margins have recovered to 15.6 per cent in FY26 from a trough of 14 per cent in FY24. The brokerage also pointed to median revenue growth of 22 per cent year-on-year in the April-June 2026 quarter, with more than 80 per cent of companies in its coverage universe reporting higher sales. 
 The recovery, however, has not been entirely volume-driven. The report noted that better realisations, stronger utilisation and an improved product mix supported the rebound, but some of the price-led growth also reflected sharp swings in crude oil and freight costs during the quarter. That makes the next few quarters important, as analysts will be watching whether growth is sustained by actual demand rather than temporary pricing support. 
 Why the long-term story still appeals to investors 
Equirus estimates the Indian speciality chemicals market at about $36 billion in 2025 and expects it to expand at roughly 11 per cent annually to around $61 billion by 2030. The brokerage said the opportunity is being shaped by domestic demand, the China+1 supply-chain shift, European plant closures and ongoing import substitution. New-age applications such as semiconductors and battery chemicals are also emerging as additional demand engines. 
Those themes have helped keep the sector on investor watchlists despite the recent downcycle. India’s semiconductor demand is projected to nearly double to more than $100 billion by 2030, while battery chemicals are expected to open another avenue for specialised suppliers, according to the report. For listed players, that could mean a longer runway if they can scale capacity efficiently and protect margins through the next cycle. 
 Policy support adds another layer of optimism 
Government policy is also being read as supportive. In the Union Budget FY27 , the Centre announced a scheme to set up three dedicated chemical parks through a challenge-based selection process, with an allocation of ₹600 crore. Balaji Amines said in its FY26 annual report that this was the first targeted budget support for chemical park infrastructure and that the move could strengthen domestic manufacturing, improve supply-chain integration and reduce import dependence. 
For the sector, the policy signal is as important as the near-term earnings recovery. Chemical parks can lower logistics friction, create industrial clustering benefits and improve access to common infrastructure, all of which matter in a business where scale and operating efficiency often decide winners over a full cycle. 
 Risks remain despite the upbeat setup 
Even with the improving backdrop, Equirus flagged several risks that could slow the recovery. These include US tariffs, volatility in crude prices, dumping from China and the speed at which newly added capacity gets absorbed. If utilisation lags, the expected improvement in return on capital may take longer to show up. 
That is why Tuesday’s sharp stock moves should be read as a bet on execution rather than a simple sentiment trade. Investors appear to be rewarding signs of a cyclical bottom, but the sector’s next leg will depend on whether the earnings rebound broadens into sustained volume growth and whether companies can monetise the capacity they have already built. 
For now, the market is signalling that speciality chemicals are back in focus. Whether the rally extends will depend on how quickly the operating recovery turns from a tentative rebound into a durable upcycle.

docs.title: Adani Power gains 2% after signing pact for 770-MW hydropower project in Bhutan
docs.text:
Shares of Adani Power gained 2% on Tuesday to hit a day’s high of Rs 205 on the NSE after the company signed a shareholder agreement (SHA) with Druk Green Power Corporation ( DGPC ) to set up the 770-MW Chamkharchhu Hydropower Project in Thimphu, Bhutan.
 Under the SHA, Adani Power and DGPC will jointly incorporate a public company in Bhutan, with a 49:51 shareholding, to undertake the project, according to a release filed with the exchange.
The project is the second major hydropower collaboration between the two partners, following the 570-MW Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project agreement signed in September 2025. It is also part of a broader 5,000-MW hydropower development MoU signed between the Adani Group and DGPC in May 2025.
 Also Read | Trent shares hit 10% upper circuit after Q2 revenue rises 23% YoY to Rs 4,724 crore. Should you buy, sell or hold? 
Located in central Bhutan’s Zhemgang district on the Chamkarchhu River, the peaking run-of-river project will be developed under the Build, Own, Operate and Transfer (BOOT) model through a 49:51 equity partnership between Adani Power and DGPC, with a 30-year concession from the date of commissioning.
 Live Events
Construction is expected to begin in the first half of 2027, with commissioning targeted within six years of groundbreaking. The project is expected to strengthen Bhutan’s clean energy capacity and regional energy cooperation.
Initially, the project company will issue 4.9 million shares to Adani Power and 5.1 million shares to DGPC at Bhutanese Ngultrum 100 per share. Both partners will have the right to appoint three directors each to the board and will make additional capital contributions in the agreed proportion as required.
The project is expected to help meet Bhutan’s peak winter electricity demand while enabling the export of surplus green power to India during the summer months.
“We are delighted to strengthen our partnership with the Royal Government of Bhutan and DGPC through the Chamkharchhu Hydroelectric Project,” said Anil Sardana, Managing Director, Adani Power. He said hydropower will play a key role in South Asia’s energy transition and the project will contribute to energy security, lower carbon intensity and shared sustainability goals.
Dasho Chhewang Rinzin, Managing Director, DGPC, said the 770-MW Chamkharchhu-I Hydropower Project will strengthen Bhutan’s energy security, particularly during winter, while creating opportunities to export surplus clean energy to India.
Both organisations are also evaluating additional hydropower opportunities under the broader 5,000-MW development programme.
 Also Read | Kotak Mahindra Bank shares jump 4% as Q2 net advances rise 25% YoY, deposits up 23% 
 Druk Green Power Corporation
Druk Green Power Corporation (DGPC) is Bhutan’s leading renewable energy generation company and a wholly owned subsidiary of Druk Holding & Investments, the commercial arm of the Royal Government of Bhutan.

docs.title: World Bank flags oil, El Niño and global market risks to growth
docs.text:
The World Bank has raised its growth forecast for South Asia for 2026, citing resilient consumer demand and strong domestic activity despite an energy shock, while warning that persistently high oil prices, severe weather and a global market correction could pose risks to the outlook, Reuters reported.
 The World Bank now expects South Asia's economy to grow 6.9% in 2026, 60 basis points higher than its previous forecast and 10 basis points above its estimate a year earlier. The upgrade reflects stronger-than-expected consumption momentum, with government measures, robust remittances and resilient domestic demand helping economies absorb the impact of higher energy costs, the World Bank said, Reuters reported.

 Read more: Global Market: Nikkei rises as Wall Street gains, oil prices fall 
The region, which relies heavily on energy imports, has so far shown greater resilience than expected to supply disruptions stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran. However, the World Bank warned that a prolonged period of elevated oil prices could eventually weigh on economic activity and inflation.
India, South Asia's largest economy, is expected to grow 7.1% in 2026/27, according to the World Bank, up from its June forecast of 6.6%. The projection is nevertheless well below the 8.6% growth recorded in 2025/26.
 Live Events
Economic activity in India has remained relatively strong even as higher inflation has reduced consumers' purchasing power. The World Bank expects inflation to remain elevated into 2027, with the impact on growth potentially taking time to emerge. In emerging markets, the typical lag between an inflationary shock and its effect on economic activity is around 18 months, the bank said.
Read more: Global Market | Central banks face tougher crisis-management role as public debt rises: BIS chief 
The World Bank has not provided an aggregate inflation forecast for South Asia for 2026 but has issued individual country projections. India's central bank expects inflation to average 5% in the current financial year.
The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on October 7, according to a Reuters poll of economists, marking its first rate increase since 2023. Economists also expect another hike in December as policymakers respond to persistent inflationary pressures.
Reuters reported that the expected rate increase would come as policymakers balance inflation risks against the resilience of economic growth.
Weather poses another potential threat to the region's growth outlook. A strong El Niño could hurt India in particular because agriculture plays an important role in rural demand and has a significant influence on food inflation. India last experienced El Niño conditions in 2023, when monsoon rainfall was about 95% of the long-period average.
The World Bank also highlighted artificial intelligence as an important avenue for sustaining growth and creating jobs over the medium term. AI adoption across South Asia remains below levels seen in advanced economies but is increasing rapidly, the bank said.
India, which accounts for a substantial share of the region's economic expansion, has seen 23% of firms report using AI, compared with 43% of US firms. The World Bank said wider adoption of the technology could help boost productivity and support the creation of more and better jobs as the region seeks to maintain its growth momentum.
The World Bank's upgraded forecast underscores the region's continued resilience, but the outlook remains vulnerable to prolonged energy price pressures, adverse weather and a sharp correction in global financial markets.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.

By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

Shares of Godrej Consumer Products gained nearly 2% in opening trade on Tuesday after the company projected high-teens revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA growth for Q2 FY27.
The stock was trading at Rs852.45, up 1.85%, at 10:17 am on the NSE. Consolidated underlying volume growth is expected at high-single-digit, while standalone revenue growth is likely in the teens despite an estimated 100-150 basis point impact from trade inventory correction.
Indonesia is expected to post high-teens revenue growth with high-single-digit volume growth, while GAUM is likely to deliver robust double-digit revenue and volume growth.
The company said input cost pressures intensified during the quarter, particularly across crude-linked derivatives, palm oils and other commodities. It is responding through calibrated pricing, cost savings, supply-chain efficiencies and disciplined cost management.
"We remain firmly on track to deliver our guidance for the full year with the confidence to exceed the same in select areas through a broad-based performance across businesses," the company said.
 Nomura retains 'Buy', target price Rs 1,110 
Nomura retained its 'Buy' rating and target price of Rs 1,110, saying the Q2 update was "a tad better than our expectations on both sales and EBITDA growth despite the inventory correction that the company had indicated earlier."
The brokerage expects consolidated revenue growth of around 17% year-on-year and EBITDA growth of around 12.5% in Q2FY27, ahead of its estimates of 15% and 9%, respectively.
India sales growth is expected at around 13%, with volume growth at 7%, despite the inventory correction. Pricing growth increased to 6% in Q2 from 4.5% in Q1, and Nomura expects it to rise to high-single-digits in coming quarters.
Nomura expects Indonesia to deliver high-single-digit volume growth and high-teens revenue growth, while GAUM growth is estimated at 15% in constant currency and over 30% including currency benefits.
The brokerage expects consolidated margins at around 19%, down 80 basis points year-on-year, and said GCPL is "tracking ahead of its guidance thus far in terms of sales but could see pressure on margins."
Nomura expects EPS CAGR of 12% over FY26-29F and continues to value GCPL through SoTP with a target price of Rs1,110.

Sterlite Technologies shares extended their winning streak to a fifth consecutive session on Tuesday, October 6, rising 3.2 percent in early trade after Nomura initiated coverage on the stock with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of Rs 1,350 per share.
The stock rose to Rs 1,033 in early trade, taking its gains over the past five sessions to nearly 25 percent. At the current price, Sterlite Technologies has a market capitalisation of around Rs 52,700 crore.
Nomura's target price implies an upside of around 35 percent from Monday's closing price of Rs 1,001.25.
The brokerage expects strong industry tailwinds to drive robust growth at Sterlite Technologies, forecasting revenue and EBITDA to grow at compound annual growth rates of 50 percent and 89 percent, respectively, over FY26-FY29.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
Nomura expects robust data-centre capacity additions, coupled with constrained supply, to drive what it sees as an optical fibre cable (OFC) demand supercycle. Sterlite Technologies is well placed to capitalise on this demand given its integrated manufacturing capacity, according to the brokerage.
The latest brokerage call comes after a sharp run-up in the stock. Sterlite Technologies shares have risen nearly tenfold so far in 2026, gaining about 879 percent on a year-to-date basis, compared with a 13.7 percent decline in the Nifty 50.
The recent rally has also been supported by large order wins. Last week, Sterlite Technologies announced a long-term supply agreement worth $1.2 billion with a hyperscale partner for optical connectivity products. The arrangement runs through December 2030, with supplies allocated in each calendar year beginning in 2026 and purchase orders to be realised periodically.
The agreement also provides for a reciprocal risk-sharing framework covering liabilities in the event of demand or supply-capacity shortfalls or failures.
The announcement followed another order-related development involving STL Networks, which emerged as the L1 bidder for a Rs 250 crore RailTel Corporation of India contract. The project involves the design, supply, installation and deployment of cloud infrastructure at RailTel's data centre and disaster-recovery site.
Sterlite Technologies shares had closed 4.8 percent higher at Rs 1,001.25 on Monday, before extending their gains on Tuesday.

On the sectoral front, Nifty Realty Index fell 0.7%, Nifty IT index shed 0.6% and Nifty PSU Bank index declined 0.3%. On the other hand, Nifty Bank, Consumer Durable, Energy, Infra, Media, FMCG, Metal, Pharma, Oil & Gas and Private Bank, Telecom up 0.5-2%.

More than 100 stocks touched 52-week low, including Max Healthcare, IOC, Bharti Hexacom, Bikaji Foods, Bombay Burmah, Max Financial, NSDL, IOC, Avenue Supermarts, among others. Click to View More 
Also Read - RBI MPC meeting October 2026: 25 bps or 50 bps hike - how far could rates go? 
Among individual stocks, Transrail Lighting shares added 4.5% on winning new orders worth Rs 412 crore, share price of Kotak Mahindra Bank jumped 3.5% after Q2 net advances jumped 24.7% and deposits increased 23.2%.
Share price of IndusInd Bank rose nearly 3% after Q2 business data, Sterlite Technologies shares touched 52-week high after Nomura initiated Buy with a target price Rs 1,350/share, while Trent shares surged 12% after Q2 standalone revenue surged 23%.

Among other stocks, Dabur India shares rose nearly 3% on double-digit growth in Q2 FY27, Bondada Engineering shares added 4% after receiving EPC order aggregating to ₹1,153.93 crore, share price of Rentomojo rose 8.5% despite Q1 profit fell 38.6%, while Steamhouse India added 10% as Q1 profit zoomed 80%, while share price of LCC Projects fell 2% after Q1 profit fell 17% and revenue declined 15%.
Share price of Axis Bank gained 2% after Q2 gross advances increased 22.7% and Vedanta rose 3% ahead of board meeting on October 8. Share price of BGR Energy added 5% after the company entered into a Master Restructuring Agreement with NARCL for restructuring outstanding debt of Rs 3,736 crore.

SRIT India shares gained 19% to end at Rs 155 on their listing day. The stock debuted at Rs 148 on the NSE, a premium of nearly 14% over the IPO price of Rs 130 per share.
Shah Investor’s Home shares rose 4% to close at Rs 174 after listing at Rs 171, a premium of more than 2% over its IPO price of Rs 167 per share.
 Shrikant Chouhan, Head Equity Research, Kotak Securities 
Today, the benchmark indices continued their pullback. The Nifty ended 220 points higher, while the Sensex gained 685 points. Among the sectoral indices, Capital Market and Chemicals rallied by over 2.44 percent, while IT shed nearly 2 percent.
Technically, the market opened higher and maintained positive momentum throughout the day. A bullish candle on the daily chart and a continuing pullback formation on the intraday chart indicate the potential for further upside from current levels.
For day traders, 22,600/72,500 will act as a key support zone. As long as the market holds above this zone, the pullback is likely to continue. On the upside, the market could rebound to 22,950–23,000/73,300–73,500. Conversely, a fall below 22,600/72,500 would make the uptrend vulnerable. Below this level, the market could slip to 22,500–22,450/72,200–72,000.

 How Bajaj Broking’s TradingView Integration Helps Traders Analyse, Execute and Manage Trades
 A good trading decision depends on two things: identifying the right opportunity and executing it at the right time.

 A trader can spend a long time studying a chart before finally deciding that a setup looks worth acting on. But spotting the opportunity is only half the job. The next few steps: placing the order, setting the risk level and managing the position; matter just as much. 
That is why the line between charting and execution has become thinner. Traders increasingly expect to analyse a setup and act on it without switching between multiple screens. Bajaj Broking’s integration with TradingView brings these functions closer together, allowing users to study price action, place orders and manage positions from the same interface.
Let’s look at how these features work and how they can help traders manage the journey from analysing a setup to executing a trade.
 Buy/Sell Buttons and Order Placement Directly from the Chart 
A good trading decision depends on two things: identifying the right opportunity and executing it at the right time.
A trader may spot a breakout, a reversal or a support level on the chart, but moving between multiple screens to place an order can create unnecessary friction. Modern trading platforms are reducing this gap by bringing chart analysis and execution closer together.
Bajaj Broking’s integration with TradingView allows traders to analyse price movements, apply technical tools and place orders directly from the TradingView interface. This allows traders to use the chart not only for analysis but also as a workspace for managing trades.
 Orders and Positions Shown Live on the Chart, With Drag-to-Modify 
Once a trade is placed, the next challenge is managing it.
TradingView allows traders to view active orders and positions directly on the chart, including entry levels, stop-loss and target prices. This gives traders a clearer picture of how their trade is positioned against the ongoing price movement.
For example, a trader can view both the entry level of ₹500 and the stop-loss of ₹480 directly on the chart instead of switching to a separate order window.
The drag-to-modify feature makes adjustments simpler. If the stock moves higher and the trader wants to shift the stop-loss from ₹480 to ₹490, the order level can be modified visually on the chart.
The tool does not replace decision-making; it simply helps traders manage the execution process more efficiently.
 Advanced Order Ticket and Bracket Order UI for Structured Entries 
TradingView’s advanced order ticket allows traders to plan these parameters while analysing the chart.
Depending on the strategy, traders can use different order types:
Market orders are used when immediate execution is the priority. For example, if a trader wants to enter a stock at the market rate, a market order allows participation at the available market price.
Limit orders allow traders to define the price at which they want to buy or sell.
Stop orders are generally used when traders want confirmation before entering a position.
For example, if a trader identifies ₹1,050 as a breakout level, a buy stop order above that level can be used. The order gets activated only when the stock crosses the specified price.
Bracket orders help traders structure a trade before entering it by combining:
For example, a trader entering after a breakout can define the entry, profit target and maximum acceptable loss beforehand.
This approach helps bring more discipline to trade management by reducing the need to make exit decisions after emotions come into play.
With Bajaj Broking’s TradingView-powered trading experience, traders can combine chart analysis with order management tools within the same platform workflow.
 Managing Trades Without Leaving the Chart 
One of the key advantages of an integrated TradingView experience is that traders can analyse and manage trades from the same interface.

This reduces the gap between spotting an opportunity and acting on it.
 Depth of Market (DOM): Understanding the Orders Behind the Price 
A stock’s last traded price shows where the latest transaction happened, but it does not reveal the buyers and sellers waiting around that price.
This is where Depth of Market (DOM), also known as the order book, becomes useful.
DOM provides visibility into pending buy and sell orders at different price levels, helping traders understand where demand and supply may be concentrated.
Traditional market depth generally provides visibility into a limited number of bid and ask levels. With deeper order book visibility through Bajaj Broking’s TradingView-integrated platform, traders can observe a wider range of price levels and understand where larger buying or selling interest may exist.
For active traders, the DOM is useful for analysing breakout attempts and assessing liquidity before placing larger orders.

 Summary
 MarketSmith India reveals its top stock recommendations for today, 7 October. Get expert insights into the best-performing stocks to guide your investment decisions.

 Stock market recap: On Tuesday, Indian equities extended their recovery for a second straight session as softer crude oil prices, firm Asian markets, and strong quarterly business updates lifted sentiment ahead of the RBI's policy decision. Nifty 50 rose 220.35 points, or 0.98%, to close at 22,776.10, finishing at its high of the day, while Sensex gained 685.34 points, or 0.95%, to settle at 73,067.81. 
 Buying was broad-based, led by capital goods, FMCG, Oil and Gas, and Healthcare stocks. Nifty IT was the only major sector to end lower, falling nearly 1%. Trent was the standout, jumping about 13% to a two-year high after reporting 23% revenue growth for the quarter. 
 Kotak Mahindra Bank rose nearly 4% on strong growth in loans and deposits, helping private banks support the index. Consumer stocks such as Dabur , Godrej Consumer, and HUL gained on signs of improving demand, especially in rural areas.
 Market breadth was strongly positive, with 2,455 stocks advancing, 1,125 stocks declining, and 115 remaining unchanged. Investors are now awaiting Wednesday's RBI policy announcement. Markets will look closely for any signal of rate hikes, which could set the near-term direction after a long losing streak.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: SKY GOLD AND DIAMONDS LIMITED (current price: ₹ 858) 
 Why it’s recommended : Strong expansion in jewellery manufacturing capacity and growing relationships with large retail chains are driving volume growth and market penetration. Rising demand for organized gold jewellery, along with increasing franchise/showroom presence, supports revenue scalability and brand visibility. 
 Key metrics : P/E: 37.28, 52-week high: ₹ 877.00, volume: ₹ 355.54 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: High dependence on gold prices exposes margins and working capital requirements to commodity price volatility. Customer concentration risk: A significant portion of revenue comes from a limited number of large jewellery retailers. 
 Buy: ₹ 849–862 
 Target price : ₹ 950 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 817 
 Buy: Black Box Limited (current price: ₹ 840) 
 Why it’s recommended: Growing demand for digital infrastructure, data center networking, cloud connectivity, and cybersecurity solutions is supporting order inflows across global markets. Strong presence in enterprise communication and IT networking services, coupled with cross-selling opportunities from large international clients, enhances long-term growth prospects. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 50.09, 52-week high: ₹ 1,103.00, volume: ₹ 92.80 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Business performance is exposed to slowdown in enterprise IT spending and delays in large technology infrastructure projects. Significant overseas operations create risks related to currency fluctuations, geopolitical developments, and client concentration in key markets. 
 Buy at: ₹ 832–844 
 Target price: ₹ 970 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 792

 On 6 October, Indian equities ended firmly higher, extending the recovery from the previous session. Nifty 50 gained 220.35 points, or 0.98%, to 22,776.10, finishing at the day’s high after opening at 22,603.25 and holding above its previous close of 22,555.75. Sensex also traded strongly, supported by improving risk appetite. Market breadth was notably positive, with 2,455 stocks advancing, 1,125 stocks declining, and 115 remaining unchanged. This translates into an advance-decline ratio of about 2.18:1 and indicates broad participation beyond index heavyweights. On the sectoral front, Pharma (+1.66%), Oil & Gas (+1.58%), Private Banks (+1.41%), and FMCG (+1.40%) led gains. On the other hand, T (-0.59%), Realty (-0.27%), and PSU Banks (-0.08%) lagged. Trent was among the standout gainers while technology counters remained under pressure. 
 Nifty 50 staged a strong rebound, closing at 22,776.10, up 0.98%, after the recent sharp decline. Despite the recovery, the broader price structure remains bearish, with the index continuing to trade below its key short-, medium-, and long-term moving averages. Price action has also moved below the previously established rising trendline, indicating weakening broader trend. The latest bounce therefore appears corrective at this stage rather than a confirmed trend reversal. 
 The RSI has recovered to 36.31 from oversold territory moved above its signal average of around 31, suggesting downside momentum is easing. The scope for a near-term recovery has improved. However, the RSI remains below the neutral 50 mark, keeping the underlying momentum bias weak. Meanwhile, the MACD remains firmly below the zero line, with the MACD line still below the signal line, confirming the prevailing negative trend. 
 Nifty 50 extended its winning streak and closed above 22,700, reflecting continued recovery momentum. On the downside, 22,200–22,000 remains a crucial support area. A sustained break below this band could renew selling pressure and potentially drag the index toward 21,700–21,600. Conversely, further upside is likely to face resistance around 22,800–23,000, which has emerged as an important technical hurdle following the recent breakdown.

 Despite the positive close, the Nifty ended below its intraday high and remained beneath the 21-, 50-, 100-, and 200-DMAs, indicating that the broader trend remains weak. The session produced a small bullish-bodied spinning-top candle with long shadows, reflecting elevated volatility and indecision. The recovery from 22,400 is encouraging, but sustained follow-through above 22,622 is necessary to strengthen the rebound and signal that demand is gaining control after the recent decline.

MACD remained deeply negative at -359.98 and below its signal line at -296.12, while the histogram stayed negative at -63.86. This configuration indicates that bearish momentum remains dominant, with no confirmed bullish crossover or divergence visible. However, RSI’s recovery from recent lows suggests selling pressure may be stabilizing. A sustained move above 30-35 in RSI, alongside contraction in the negative MACD histogram, would provide the earliest evidence of momentum improvement.
 Immediate support is placed at 22,397, followed by 22,300 and the psychological 22,000 level. A decisive breakdown below 22,000 could extend weakness toward 21,800. Near-term rebounds may receive support from positive global equities and modest easing in crude prices. However, heavy FII selling, rupee weakness, oil remaining above $100, and elevated US Treasury yields remain substantial headwinds. Therefore, Nifty may remain volatile with a cautious bias unless it decisively reclaims 22,800–23,000 on stronger volumes and improving breadth.

docs.title: Q2 business updates: Experts tell best banking stocks to buy ahead of Q2 results FY27?
docs.text:
Market investors may be wondering whether now is the right time to invest in private-sector banking stocks. According to Seema Srivastava, Senior Research Analyst at SMC Global Securities, evaluating banking stocks after the Q2 FY27 business updates requires looking closely at deposit mobilization, credit expansion, and structural adaptations like the Reserve Bank of India’s FCNR(B) swap facility across major financial institutions. 
Experts also assess which banking stocks could be worth considering ahead of the Q2 results season.
 The bank showed robust period-end deposit growth of 18.8% year-on-year, reaching ₹ 33,275 billion, alongside gross advances growth of 16.3% year-on-year, touching ₹ 32,195 billion. The bank effectively leveraged its market scale by mobilizing $11.5 billion in foreign currency non-resident deposits, maintaining healthy balance sheet momentum and steady granular deposit acquisition. 
 Axis Bank delivered strong momentum with gross advances growing 22.7% year-on-year to ₹ 13,846 billion and total deposits rising 20.7% year-on-year to ₹ 14,521 billion. Even when excluding FCNR(B)-backed leverage operations, Axis Bank's core gross advances expanded by a solid 18.8% year-on-year. 
Yes Bank demonstrated healthy business traction as net advances expanded 23.8% year-on-year to ₹ 309,675 crore and deposits grew 19.5% year-on-year to ₹ 354,084 crore. Yes Bank's normalized advances growth stood at 17.7% year-on-year, with its credit-to-deposit ratio improving to a healthier 87.5%.
 Kotak Mahindra Bank displayed aggressive expansion, reporting a net advances surge of 24.7% year-on-year to ₹ 5,77,094 crore and total deposit growth of 23.2% year-on-year to ₹ 6,51,491 crore, bolstered significantly by $5.78 billion in FCNR(B) inflows. 
IDBI Bank recorded steady, broad-based growth, with total business crossing ₹ 6.27 lakh crore representing an 18% year-on-year increase, net advances reaching ₹ 2,71,537 crore up 18% year-on-year, and total deposits expanding 17% year-on-year to ₹ 355,611 crore.
IndusInd Bank reported more moderate metrics, with net advances moving up 11.2% year-on-year to ₹ 3,62,393 crore and deposits rising 10.1% year-on-year to ₹ 4,29,038 crore. However, its CASA ratio moderated to 28.0%, reflecting ongoing industry-wide pressure on low-cost liability mobilization.
Srivastava recommended long-term investors should aim for compounding, stability, and lower portfolio volatility should note that large-cap private sector heavyweights remain fundamentally superior. 
 She added that HDFC Bank stands out as the primary compounder for long-term holding. Its massive liability franchise and continuous deposit outperformance provide structural insulation against broader liquidity squeezes. 
 “Simultaneously, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Axis Bank offer aggressive growth profiles backed by high-quality capital adequacy, making them strong alternatives for long-term capital appreciation. Conversely, mid-tier and turnaround candidates carry higher execution or asset-quality risks over extended horizons compared to these top-tier institutional compounders,” she added. 
 Meanwhile, Sugandha Sachdeva, Founder of SS WealthStreet, while picking Kotak Mahindra Bank as the top stock to buy, said that the stock is looking constructive following its Q2 FY27 business update, with the stock witnessing a strong rebound from lower levels on healthy volumes. 
Sachdeva explained that the the stock is sustaining above its key moving averages and continues to form a higher-high, higher-low structure, indicating improving momentum. The recent rise has also been accompanied by strong volumes, adding conviction to the recovery.
On the technical outlook, she added, "In the short term, the stock appears to have established a base around Rs.386, while from a medium-term perspective, Rs.350 remains a stronger structural support zone. As long as these levels hold, the broader trend remains positive.
On the upside, the stock has the potential to retest the Rs.460 zone, which is close to its previous lifetime-high region. A decisive breakout above Rs.460 could open the way for a further move towards Rs.505-525 over the medium to long term."

docs.title: IPO mutual funds: How do fund managers buy and sell shares at pre- and post-listing stages? Experts explain
docs.text:
Examples include Edelweiss Recently Listed IPO Fund and Mirae Asset BSE Select IPO ETF. While one is an active fund that gives the fund manager flexibility to select stocks, the other is a passive fund that tracks an index. But how do fund managers actually buy and sell IPO stocks, and what should investors look at when evaluating these funds? Uttam Agarwal, Chief Business Officer at Bajaj Capital, mentioned that “for a fund manager, the real work starts much before the listing. Fund managers study the offer documents, meet the management and look at the business, financials, promoter track record and, importantly, whether the valuation makes sense”. Once they decide to invest, position sizing becomes important. With a newly listed company, there is limited market history, so a manager may start with a measured allocation and increase it as the business delivers and the investment case gets stronger. The same thinking applies to exits. A stock going up isn't automatically a reason to sell. If the business continues to perform and the valuation remains reasonable, there may be merit in staying invested. If the fundamentals or valuation change, the manager can reassess, he explained. Manish P. Hingar, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Fintoo, explained that the IPO-focused mutual funds can buy IPO shares at different stages: “Buying shares from unlisted markets before the IPO is launched doesn't apply here since it is a different type of investment activity,” Piyush Jhunjhunwala, Founder and CEO, Stockify, added. An exit from a position will not typically be dictated simply by financial results. The fund manager will continue tracking the stock's valuation, the prospects for its earnings, its cash flows, the way it operates, its competition, and its corporate developments, Jhunjhunwala added. A stock may be sold even after strong returns if its valuation runs ahead of expected earnings growth. Weakening business prospects, poor earnings visibility, governance concerns, or a change in the investment thesis can also prompt an exit, he added. “Portfolio turnover will depend on the investment philosophy of the fund and the current market environment. However, high turnover in itself cannot be seen as a positive,” Jhunjhunwala noted. The mainboard is likely to remain the larger opportunity set for most IPO-focused strategies because these companies generally offer greater scale, disclosure, and liquidity. Whether a particular fund can invest in SME IPOs depends on its mandate, Agarwal mentioned. An IPO fund is better viewed as a small addition to an equity portfolio rather than a core holding. Investors should look beyond returns and popular IPOs and check the portfolio’s sector exposure, number of holdings, allocation to newly listed stocks, valuations and concentration, Hingar said. Investors should also assess whether the portfolio reflects the fund’s stated strategy, including its market-cap and recent-listing exposure. Don't judge portfolio based on listing day gains, Agarwal said. Expense ratio, portfolio turnover ratio, downside risk and consistency of returns are also useful indicators. Investors should also check how much of the fund is actually invested in newly listed and IPO companies, Jhunjhunwala added. Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. docs.title: Monster, PepsiCo and Campa gets interim relief over ‘energy drink’ label, but cannot make more
docs.text:
News Monster, PepsiCo and Campa gets interim relief over ‘energy drink’ label, but cannot make more Yash Tiwari , Neethi Lisa Rojan 3 min read 6 Oct 2026, 06:38 PM IST Summary Monster Energy, PepsiCo and Reliance Consumer Products have won interim relief from the Delhi High Court against FSSAI's move to stop beverage makers from using the term ‘energy drink’ on certain caffeinated products. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now Three consumer firms—Monster Energy, PepsiCo and Reliance Consumer Products—secured stay orders from the Delhi High Court on Tuesday against Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) directions restricting the use of the term ‘energy drink’ for their products. The relief came as the high court was hearing different pleas filed by the companies challenging the FSSAI orders passed in June and July. The regulator had directed manufacturers to stop using the ‘energy drink’ descriptor on certain caffeinated beverages and warned of enforcement action. In a post on a social media platform on 1 July, FSSAI said it has “issued notices to several beverage brands claiming to be ‘energy drinks’ for misbranding and misleading claims.” The regulator named brands, including Red Bull Energy Drink, PepsiCo India's Adrenaline Rush Energy Drink, Sting Energy Drink, Monster Energy, Hell-Energy Drink, and Reliance's Campa Energy Drink–Gold Boost, for using the descriptor ‘energy drink’ on physical packaging and across various e-commerce platforms. FSSAI said its food category system is not intended for product naming or labelling. It also said claims such as ‘stimulates mind’, ‘energises body’, ‘enhances focus’, ‘boosts energy levels’ and ‘aids in general weakness’ were not permissible unless legally supported. Counsel appearing for Monster Energy argued that their products had been licensed under the relevant food categories and that FSSAI itself had earlier clarified that the term ‘energy drink’ was permitted for products falling within those categories. He also added that the decision taken by FSSAI did not allow the company to respond to the notices which were served. The Delhi High Court on 29 September set aside the notice served to Red Bull over ‘ energy drink’ labelling, holding that the company should have been given an opportunity to respond before the regulator passed the order. Email queries sent by Mint to Monster, PepsiCo and Reliance Consumer were not answered till presstime. According to the order copy seen by Mint , the court cleared that the manufacturers are allowed to sell the stock which is manufactured till today with the description ‘energy drink’ and have to keep the records for the same. The court also stated that the interim order should not be interpreted to mean that the manufacturers are permitted to produce the packaging with the terms “Energy Drink”. “... order granting stay, however, shall not be interpreted to have permitted the bottlers/contractors of the petitioner to further manufacture the product with the terms 'Energy Drink'", the order copy stated. Companies flag inventory impact Beverage manufacturer PepsiCo, represented by Sandeep Sethi, told the court that the FSSAI action was already affecting how its products were sold, including on e-commerce platforms. Sethi pointed out that the regulator’s directions were being communicated to online platforms, potentially affecting the sale of products already in the market. Monster also made a similar argument by informing the court that ‘30 million units are on the street’ while explaining the impact of the order. On the contrary, FSSAI submitted that they had a meeting with the industry member on 20 July, to discontinue the use of the ‘energy drink’ descriptor in future production. FSSAI relied on the minutes of that meeting and said Monster was among the participants. Reliance’s Campa was also hit with a similar notice as it tried to make its way into the Indian beverage market. According to a Reuters report, Reliance holds finished inventory of 168 million cans and 120 million plastic bottles, along with pre-printed packaging for an additional 400 million cans and 360 million bottles bearing the ‘Energy Drink’ labelling, it said in its October filing. India’s energy drinks market is expanding rapidly. Euromonitor estimates retail sales are growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China. The market is expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028. All three pleas will be taken up for hearing on 5 November.  In China, battle is raging for the soul of Tibet
 Jonathan Cheng , The Wall Street Journal 7 min read 6 Oct 2026, 06:42 AM IST 
 Summary
 On the edge of the Himalayas, a tourist boomtown sells Chinese visitors a commoditized, politically palatable version of Tibetan culture. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 SHANGRI-LA, China—When China’s masses want to experience the Tibet of chanting, crimson-robed monks and prayer flags flapping in the wind, they don’t go to Tibet.
 Instead, they flock to Shangri-La, a tourist boomtown in the neighboring province of Yunnan, where Tibetan culture is denuded of many of its religious elements—and any trace of the Dalai Lama’s influence—and sanitized for the country’s ethnic Han majority.
 Here, the narrow alleys of the old market town are packed with Han Chinese tourists in faux Tibetan costumes, who repurpose ancient monasteries as backdrops for social-media glamor shots.
 They throng a hilltop temple to turn the enormous 69-foot-tall golden prayer wheel, once the world’s largest. Others head to the 350-foot-tall Buddhist stupa that local officials added five years ago—conspicuously designated as a “nonreligious site.”
 Communist Party officials in Beijing are well aware of the romantic appeal of Tibetan culture, both in the West and among its own Han citizens. With the Dalai Lama—the famous monk reviled by Beijing as a separatist—now in his nineties, a fight for control of Tibetan Buddhism looms.
 Since fleeing into exile in India in 1959, he has been the center of a global Tibetan resistance movement to Chinese policies that he warns seek to “overwhelm” Tibet’s distinct identity.
 The battle for hearts and minds is being fought in places like Shangri-La, where a highly commodified, and politically palatable, version of Tibetan culture is presented to ordinary Chinese people.
 It is working.
 Even local Tibetans feel they have little choice but to join in. Outside of tourism and picking matsutake mushrooms, there are few other sources of wealth in this rugged, historically impoverished corner of China.
 After years of policies designed to more closely integrate China’s minorities into the Han-dominated mainstream, many ethnic Tibetans now say that feelings of a separate identity are quickly disappearing, with the monasteries deprived of young devotees and many Tibetans themselves struggling to read or write the language.
 Chimi Lhamo, an ethnic Tibetan makeup artist working in one of Shangri-La’s hundreds of costume photography studios, is torn about the tourist waves that have transformed her hometown. “It’s all fake, but what can we do?” she said.
 Tibetan dress-up
 Lhamo is quick to tout the economic benefits of the tourist boom that started in 2001, when local officials rechristened the city—then known as Gyalthang, or Zhongdian in Chinese—after the mythical paradise in James Hilton’s 1933 novel “Lost Horizon.”
 Within years, the city was pitching itself as an untroubled utopia in the Himalayas, where wisdom and tranquility could be found. Up went the oversized prayer wheel, followed by the oversized stupa.
 Lhamo, who was born in Shangri-La in 1997, just a few years before its tourist-minded rebranding, still remembers when the city was a one-stoplight town, poor and isolated.
 “Economic growth is a good thing,” she said. “I don’t begrudge it.”
 While Western tourists had begun to come to Shangri-La decades earlier, the domestic tourist boom began after Covid-19-era lockdowns left China’s growing middle class grappling for a sense of escape and meaning. Today, there are at least 300 costume photography studios in Shangri-La, a city of fewer than 200,000 people.
 Lhamo, who once owned her own costume studio before taking a job doing makeup for a studio run by a Han Chinese woman from outside Shangri-La, insisted on ensuring that some authentic Tibetan costumes were on offer.
 She soon learned that customers weren’t interested. “The most important thing is that it looks good in pictures,” she said. “A lot of customers will ask me if I would wear these costumes, and I tell them bluntly: ‘I would never wear this.’”
 In a society where allegations of cultural appropriation are largely absent, tourists wander the old city in costume with hired photographers in tow, posing in mock prayer or spinning handheld prayer wheels at the city’s centuries-old Ganden Sumtseling Monastery.
 In search of the real Tibet
 The Tibet Autonomous Region, which has been under Beijing’s control since 1951, is the only region in China that requires an extra travel permit for foreigners—and is one of the most tightly controlled in general, given the political sensitivities around the Dalai Lama.
 For Chinese people, traveling there is prohibitively difficult. Lhasa, the seat of the Potala Palace and for centuries the capital of the Tibetan kingdom, is one of the world’s highest-altitude cities.
 Yan Xinyi, a 22-year-old Han native of Nanjing, in China’s prosperous east, hopes to one day see the Potala Palace for herself. The next best thing, she said, was coming to Shangri-La’s Ganden Sumtseling Monastery, dressed as a Japanese anime character with vaguely Tibetan elements.
 “Han Chinese could learn from the Tibetans about their relationship with nature,” Yan said, though she also complained about Shangri-La’s overt commercialization. She singled out the city’s dozens of tusi banquets — dinner theater shows sold as exotic cultural experiences, with slickly coiffed young Tibetan men wiggling across the stage to hip-hop beats for an appreciative, largely female audience.
 Wu Shaohua, a 28-year-old from Jiangxi province, was dressed in what one imagines a Tibetan shaman might wear.
 Wu said he and his partner decided to come to Shangri-La because of the town’s slogan billing itself as “the closest place to heaven.” They found the natural scenery stunning, but ackno

 Sweat and savings: how to plan for Hyrox's associated expenses without going into debt
 Ann Jacob 6 min read 6 Oct 2026, 10:22 AM IST 
 Summary
 While competing in Hyrox offers a unique experience, the associated expenses require clear financial guardrails. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 At the Hyrox Mumbai arena inside Nesco’s Bombay Exhibition Center on September 19, the air buzzed with heavy bass, sweat and the resilient whir of weighted sleds pulled across the floor. Months of grueling preparation for indoor fitness competition paid off at the finish line as athletes collapsed in both exhaustion and exhilaration, cheered on by friends and family in the stands. 
 Behind the medals and pictures of the event lies a demanding physical—and financial—discipline that these athletes had to power through. Signing up for Hyrox with an ₹ 8,500 pass comes with the costs of specialized training, carbon-plated gear, sports nutrition, travel and recovery. These expenses recur through the months leading up to the race, inflating fitness spending and calling for proper planning of physical and financial health. 
 Plated shoes to race simulations 
 For participants, signing up for the race pass is just the opening to a much larger financial commitment. Sai Aravindh, a 25-year-old production supervisor from Coimbatore, spent four months preparing for his first Hyrox race in Bengaluru, navigating training expenses and travel costs. Besides his registration fee, Sai spent ₹ 13,000 on flight tickets, ₹ 5,000 on local transport and meals, ₹ 6,000 monthly on gym fees and up to ₹ 5,000 monthly for supplements.
 “Switching to Hyrox-specific gym and training saw my training fees more than double on a month-on-month basis compared to the usual gym and training," Aravindh explained. 
 To manage this sudden surge in costs, he allocated a portion of his monthly income directly toward fitness spending .
 “It is definitely a combination of investment and experience. The vibe during Hyrox feels surreal and makes you feel the cost you paid is worth it. It definitely is an investment in your health,” he added. 
 While some athletes opt for specialized centres, others try to keep baseline expenses low, only to encounter steep equipment and hidden operational costs. Ralph Martin Pinto, a 22-year-old former video editor from Mumbai, kept his monthly gym spend at ₹ 2,000-3,000 by using a basic facility. However, race-appropriate gear quickly inflated his budget when he bought a pair of Puma Hyrox Deviate shoes costing ₹ 22,000. 
 Partial and full-race simulations, which cost about ₹ 1,000 per session, as well as single-day spectator passes for family members added up. His initial plan to offset some costs through post-race sponsorships did not come through after sustaining a shin injury right before the event, showing sudden physical setbacks can derail both athletic performance and financial planning. 
 “Hyrox is indeed an expensive sport. The gyms are very far and super expensive, and to get into a competition, the travel cost to another city and stay, combined with the fees, is too much,” Pinto noted. 
 For Dharmil Mehta, a 31-year-old actuary based in Mumbai, preparing independently still called for some expenses. Mehta spent ₹ 10,000 on registration, ₹ 15,000 on specialized nutrition like gels, electrolytes and protein, ₹ 7,000 on training guidance, ₹ 25,000 on footwear and equipment and ₹ 5,000 on massages, viewing the expenses as an essential health investment. 
 Separating essentials from hype 
 Pooja Rajpal, co-founder of 6262 Fitness and a head judge across major Hyrox events in India, emphasizes that preparation, rather than registration, represents the largest financial commitment. 
 A basic three-month preparation cycle in a home city, combining a ₹ 11,000 entry package with 36 specialized training sessions at ₹ 900 each, carbon-plated footwear, and apparel, ranges from ₹ 65,000 to ₹ 71,000, according to Rajpal. 
 When adding structured sports nutrition guidance, monthly physiotherapy, and contrast recovery sessions, the cost climbs to ₹ 95,000 to ₹ 1,15,000. For an outstation event with flights, accommodation and meals, Rajpal calculates total expenses can easily reach ₹ 1.35 lakh-1.65 lakh. Athletes should prioritize appropriate plated footwear, adequate hydration and timely physiotherapy. 
 “Participants can avoid buying expensive Hyrox-branded apparel, multiple pairs of premium shoes, unnecessary supplements, costly gadgets, excessive paid simulations, non-essential recovery sessions and official photographs. Booking travel early can also reduce costs,” she added. 
 Guardrails, emergency fund and recovery 
 Participating in Hyrox will push lifestyle spending beyond routine gym fees, risking a drain on the household budget. Easy credit and buy-now-pay-later offers supported by partnerships may make every high-ticket aspiration feel accessible, but actually cause a leveraged lifestyle. 
 The goal isn't to say no to these ambitions, but to prioritize and plan around this, according to planners. Just like training physically and mentally for the intense event, individuals should also approach the start line with months of financial preparation. 
 Preeti Zende, an investment adviser and founder of Apna Dhan Financial Services, says budgeting should start at least six months prior to enrolling in the event. 
 Rather than relying on high-interest credit or breaking into emergency reserves, athletes should accumulate the required capital systematically. Zende highlights that monthly training expenses can exceed ₹ 10,000, making a 15-20% contingency buffer vital to cover unexpected costs.

docs.title: Bond laddering: a simple way to manage interest-rate risk
docs.text:
Mint Money Bond laddering: a simple way to manage interest-rate risk Jash Kriplani 2 min read 6 Oct 2026, 12:10 PM IST Summary Bond laddering spreads a lump-sum investment across instruments with different maturities, helping investors manage reinvestment risk while creating a regular flow of cash. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now When you invest a large sum in bonds or fixed deposits (FDs), you have to pick a tenure. Lock in for five years and you may miss out if rates rise later. Stay short and you may have to reinvest at lower rates if they fall. Bond laddering offers a simple way to navigate both risks. In a ladder, you split your money across several bonds or deposits that mature at different times, usually a year or so apart. Each maturity is one "rung" of the ladder. Say you have ₹ 10 lakh. You don't put all of it in a five-year bond. Instead, you put ₹ 2 lakh each into instruments maturing in one, two, three, four and five years. When the one-year rung matures, you reinvest that ₹ 2 lakh in a new five-year instrument. After the first few years, one part of your money matures every year, and each new rung earns the longer-tenure rate. Rate protection The main benefit is that you spread out your reinvestment risk. Because only part of your money comes up for reinvestment each year, you don't have to deploy the whole amount at a bad time. If rates go up, the maturing rung can be reinvested at the higher rate. If they fall, the rest of your portfolio continues to earn the older, higher rates. The second benefit is liquidity. Since something matures every year, you have a regular flow of cash for planned expenses, such as school fees or a retiree's household costs, without having to break a deposit early or sell a bond before maturity. "When interest rates rise, bond prices fall. If you have to sell a long-term bond early, you could take a loss. A ladder avoids this because a part of your money matures every year, and bonds held to maturity pay back the contracted amount," pointed out Joydeep Sen, corporate trainer ( financial markets ) and author. Where to invest You can build a ladder with bank FDs, government securities ( G-secs ) bought through the RBI Retail Direct platform, corporate bonds, state development loans or target maturity funds. Target maturity funds, which hold bonds to a fixed maturity date, make it easier for small investors to set up rungs without buying individual bonds. There are trade-offs. A ladder won't give you the highest possible return in any single year, because part of your money always sits in shorter tenures, where yields are typically lower than longer-tenure bonds. A ladder works best for investors who need predictable income or who are putting a lump sum into fixed income and don't want to bet on where interest rates are headed. Match the rungs to when you'll need the money, and stick to good-quality issuers. News Pay for performance: How India’s staffing model is getting a makeover Devina Sengupta 4 min read 7 Oct 2026, 06:00 AM IST Summary Major staffing firms Quess, TeamLease, and Adecco report that clients are shifting from flat fees to output-based billing. Vendors now manage workforce performance, facing penalties if targets are missed and earning rewards when they deliver Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now India's staffing industry is moving beyond providing workers to taking responsibility for what they deliver. This helps the client tackle inefficiencies while giving vendors scope to charge higher fees. Three of India's largest staffing firms – Quess Corp, TeamLease Services and Adecco– which together provide about a million workers to clients on a contract basis, are seeing demand for “output-based billing” instead of a flat-fee structure. Across e-commerce , logistics, agriculture, IT, and consumer sectors, clients are adopting this model, signing clauses under which the recruitment firm will lose its margin or incur a penalty if its workforce does not meet the targets set by the client. “Over the last couple of years, we have seen an output-based workforce model begin to take shape alongside the traditional general staffing model,” said Nitin Dave, chief executive officer (CEO) at Quess Staffing. “While general staffing has typically operated on a service-fee model linked to workforce deployment, companies across FMCD, logistics, e-commerce and agri-based sectors are increasingly looking at manpower solutions where commercial outcomes are linked to productivity or output.” Fast-moving consumer durables (FMCD) include long-lasting appliances like electronic items. Staff managers In recruitment parlance, staffing firms provide workers for six months to a couple of years for a flat fee that is typically 9-10% of the employee's cost to company (CTC). The worker remains on the staffing firm's payroll, not the client's. This is different from gig service providers, who offer manpower for shorter periods, and allow them to toggle between multiple client platforms, as is the case with delivery workers. In permanent recruitment , the staffing firm sources candidates and the client hires them, after a few rounds of interviews, hires the person, who is put on the company's payroll. The vendor works for a set fee that depends on the candidate's role and hierarchy. For executive search firms that headhunt top bosses, the fee structure is split into three parts: the cost of hunting the CXO, a second tranche when the candidate accepts the offer, and a final tranche paid after the CXO has stayed in the firm for six months. In between, if the candidate drops out or the CXO quits within the first six months, the search firm must restart the process at no additional cost. Now, the staffing firm is more accountable for workforce performance. “We are seeing contracts with penalty and reward clauses. If the worker is not following protocols which may impact the business and safety of the workplace, the vendor’s fees may get slashed,” said Sunil Chemmankotil, country manager for Adecco India. Competitor Quess has also seen both penalties and rewards tied to workforce performance. “Today, around 10–15% of our clients are seeking some form of output-driven service, and we see this emerging as a new line of business for workforce solutions companies such as Quess,” said Dave. The model is still in its early stages in India, staffing firms said, but managed services, which include penalty clauses, are common practice in developed countries where supply chain demand is at a premium. In India, rising labour costs and tier-1 and tier-2 cities competing for workforce demand mean these penalty clauses help rein in absenteeism. “The margins are higher, and the recruitment vendor can manage the operations for the client and take a call on the workforce needed and where to station them, manage their expenses, take care of payroll, etc. The fees in this case can range from 10-20% per candidate versus single digital in regular staffing,” said Adecco's country manager. TeamLease Services said that with artificial intelligence (AI) driving 20-25% productivity gains in areas like development and testing, the expectation is shifting from paying for activity to paying for outcomes. In hiring, this means clients want partners to be accountable for closures, quality and time-to-hire, rather than just providing profiles. “Contracts are increasingly linking commercials to outcomes. This can include replacement commitments, SLA-based clauses, early-attrition provisions and credits linked to delivery,” said Neeti Sharma, CEO, TeamLease Digital. “Fee models are also becoming more flexible, with success-linked or milestone-based payments.” Service level agreement (SLA) is signed between the service provider and the client/customer. For staffing firms, however, the new model has yet to completely overturn the earlier business model. “The adoption is still evolving, so we would not put a single number to it. But we are seeing these conversations much more frequently, especially in high-volume and repeat hiring,” said Sharma.
